title: 新产品还在构思阶段，怎样安排测试？
topic: 把产品概念做成样品并与用户测试

source.title: Focus on product development
source.type: 乐高公开的产品开发历史资料
source.context: 乐高 乐高公开的产品开发历史资料。
paragraphs: From the late-1950s onwards the LEGO® system is becoming well established, and the market is ready for product differentiation. This means a need for more focus on product development.

A special product development department, LEGO Futura, is set up in Billund around 1959. Its employees are to concentrate on developing the product and testing their ideas together with children. LEGO Futura is organized as an independent unit, reporting directly to CEO and owner Godtfred Kirk Christiansen. Day to day management of the department is in the hands of Godtfred Kirk Christiansen’s assistant, Erik Tapdrup, who later becomes development director.

In 1969, LEGO Futura sets up a test workshop. It lets designers transform their ideas into something tangible. The workshop makes manual samples and mini tools of brass for casting specimen pieces – a breakthrough in product development. It permits much more thorough sampling and testing before individual elements are released on the market.

The LEGO Group wants to add a range of functions to its products. Trains and cars need to do more than just drive. Doll’s furniture has to have real cupboards and drawers. Older children look for a greater degree of realism – with age comes the demand that toys look like “the real thing”. The arrival of “special elements” bringing that natural appearance is the answer to what children are looking for. Surveys prove the point.

More demand for functions and realism prompts the establishment of an “element committee” whose job it is to safeguard the LEGO System’s basic idea. The committee submits each new element for examination to make sure it fits the LEGO System in Play. Most of the new specialized elements have a degree of flexibility. For example, a hinge or a cog can be used in many different connections appealing to children's imagination and creativity.
translations: 从 20 世纪 50 年代末开始，乐高系统逐渐成熟，市场开始需要产品差异化，因此公司需要更加重视产品开发。
约在 1959 年，乐高在比隆成立了专门的产品开发部门 LEGO Futura，员工专注于产品开发，并和儿童一起测试创意。该部门作为独立单位运作，直接向 CEO 兼所有者 Godtfred Kirk Christiansen 汇报。部门日常由他的助理 Erik Tapdrup 管理；Tapdrup 后来成为开发总监。
1969 年，乐高建立了测试工作坊，让设计师把创意做成实物。工作坊会制作手工样品，并用小型黄铜工具浇铸样品部件——这在产品开发上是一项突破。设计师因此能在单个零件上市前进行更充分的取样和测试。
乐高希望产品拥有更多功能：火车和汽车不能只会行驶，玩偶家具也要有真正的柜子和抽屉。年纪更大的孩子希望玩具更逼真，随着年龄增长，他们会希望玩具看起来像“真的”。增加能带来自然外观的特殊零件，回应了孩子的需求；调查也证实了这一点。
对功能和逼真度的需求不断增加，促使乐高成立“零件委员会”，负责维护乐高系统的基本理念。委员会会审查每一种新零件，确保它符合乐高游戏系统。许多新零件还能灵活组合，例如铰链或齿轮可以用于多种连接方式，激发孩子的想象力和创造力。
fullTextParagraphs: From the late-1950s onwards the LEGO® system is becoming well established, and the market is ready for product differentiation. This means a need for more focus on product development.

A special product development department, LEGO Futura, is set up in Billund around 1959. Its employees are to concentrate on developing the product and testing their ideas together with children. LEGO Futura is organized as an independent unit, reporting directly to CEO and owner Godtfred Kirk Christiansen. Day to day management of the department is in the hands of Godtfred Kirk Christiansen’s assistant, Erik Tapdrup, who later becomes development director.
A second development department is opened in Copenhagen in 1974.

In 1969, LEGO Futura sets up a test workshop. It lets designers transform their ideas into something tangible. The workshop makes manual samples and mini tools of brass for casting specimen pieces – a breakthrough in product development. It permits much more thorough sampling and testing before individual elements are released on the market.

One of the products developed by LEGO Futura is the first LEGO train with rails and a 4.5-volt motor launched in 1966. Development continues, and 1969 sees the arrival of 12-volt trains with power skid, powered rails and transformer.

The LEGO Group wants to add a range of functions to its products. Trains and cars need to do more than just drive. Doll’s furniture has to have real cupboards and drawers. Older children look for a greater degree of realism – with age comes the demand that toys look like “the real thing”. The arrival of “special elements” bringing that natural appearance is the answer to what children are looking for. Surveys prove the point.

More demand for functions and realism prompts the establishment of an “element committee” whose job it is to safeguard the LEGO System’s basic idea. The committee submits each new element for examination to make sure it fits the LEGO System in Play. Most of the new specialized elements have a degree of flexibility. For example, a hinge or a cog can be used in many different connections appealing to children's imagination and creativity.

notes.phrase: testing their ideas together with children
notes.explain: 用户测试帮助团队确认创意是否符合真实需要。
notes.example: We should test the idea with customers before launch.

notes.phrase: transform their ideas into something tangible
notes.meaning: turn an idea into a sample
notes.explain: 先把概念做成能试用的东西，再收集反馈。
notes.example: The prototype turns the idea into something tangible.

notes.explain: 调查结果可以作为判断用户需求的依据。
notes.example: Survey results support the case for a smaller package.

scenario.title: 模拟新品评估：先做样品还是直接量产？
english: Your team has an idea for a new reusable lunch container.
Customers want it to fit in a small bag and keep food from leaking.
You need to propose a sample test and say what feedback will guide the next decision.
chinese: 团队有一个新款可重复使用午餐盒的想法。
顾客希望它能放进小包里，同时避免食物漏出。
你需要提出样品测试，并说明哪些反馈将决定下一步。

firstAttempt.prompt: 模拟新品评估：顾客希望可重复使用的饭盒能放进小包且不漏。请用英语提出量产前的样品测试，并说明测试对象、时长，以及决定下一步时要看的反馈。
firstAttempt.sample: Customers need a lunch container that fits in a small bag and does not leak. Could we make a sample and test it with ten customers before moving to production? We’ll ask them to carry it in a work bag and use it for a week. We’ll review leakage, ease of cleaning, and fit before deciding what to change.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先验证需求和样品，不急着承诺量产；把测试任务和判断标准说清楚。

taskPhrases.example: Customers need a container that fits in a small bag.
taskPhrases.translation: 顾客需要一个能放进小包里的容器。

taskPhrases.word: Could we make a sample and test it with…?
taskPhrases.meaning: 我们能否先做样品并和……一起测试？
taskPhrases.example: Could we make a sample and test it with ten customers?
taskPhrases.translation: 我们能否先做样品并和十位顾客一起测试？

taskPhrases.example: We’ll review leakage and ease of cleaning before deciding what to change.
taskPhrases.translation: 我们会先检查漏不漏、是否容易清洗，再决定改什么。

words.example: We’ll test a sample before approving production.
words.translation: 批准生产前，我们会先测试样品。
words.note: 可用于产品开发、采购和质量检查。

words.example: A tangible sample helps customers react to the design.
words.translation: 具体样品能帮助顾客对设计提出反馈。
words.note: 这里指把想法做成能触摸、试用的样品。

words.example: Let’s agree on the decision criteria before the test.
words.translation: 我们在测试前先商定决策标准。
words.note: criteria 是 criterion 的复数形式。

structure.original: It lets designers transform their ideas into something tangible.
analysis: let + 人 + 动词原形，表示让某人能够做某事。
transform…into… 表示把想法转化成具体的东西。
structure.transfer: The prototype lets customers try the new booking flow before launch.

rewrite.bad: We think this product will be popular, so let’s start manufacturing it.
rewrite.good: Customers need a lunch container that fits in a small bag and does not leak. Could we make a sample and test it with ten customers before production? We’ll review leakage, ease of cleaning, and fit before deciding what to change.
rewrite.translation: 顾客需要一个能放进小包、又不会漏的午餐盒。我们能否在量产前先做样品并和十位顾客测试？我们会先检查漏不漏、是否容易清洗、尺寸是否合适，再决定改什么。
rewrite.pattern: Customers need [benefit]. Could we make a sample and test it with [group]? We’ll review [criteria] before deciding [next step].

cloze.prompt: Could we make a ______ before moving to production?
cloze.why: make a sample 表示先做一个样品。

cloze.prompt: The container ______ in a small bag.
cloze.why: fit in 表示能放进某个空间。

cloze.prompt: We’ll review leakage and ease of cleaning before deciding what to ______.
cloze.why: before deciding what to change 表示根据测试结果再决定调整内容。

dictation.text: The team tested its ideas together with children.
dictation.why: 听清 tested ideas together with，说明团队与用户一起测试。

dictation.text: The workshop made samples before products were released.
dictation.why: 注意 before 表示先后顺序：先做样品，再上市。

translationPractice.prompt: 顾客需要一个能放进小包里的容器。
translationPractice.answer: Customers need a container that fits in a small bag.
translationPractice.why: 说明产品要满足的用户需要。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否先做样品并和十位顾客一起测试？
translationPractice.answer: Could we make a sample and test it with ten customers?
translationPractice.why: 提出样品测试而不是直接量产。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们会先检查漏不漏、是否容易清洗，再决定改什么。
translationPractice.answer: We’ll review leakage and ease of cleaning before deciding what to change.
translationPractice.why: 用明确标准决定下一步改动。

choice.prompt: 新产品样品测试后，顾客喜欢外观，但多人反馈盖子容易漏。下一步最合适的是？
options: Move to mass production because customers like the design.
Adjust the lid, test the next sample with customers, and compare leakage results before approving production.
Change the product color and announce the launch date.
choice.why: 优先解决影响使用的反馈，再用下一轮样品测试确认。

output.prompt: 团队正在设计一款新的预约页面。用户担心步骤太多。请提出样品测试，并说明测试标准。
output.sample: Users need to book an appointment without entering the same details twice. Could we test a clickable prototype with six customers before development? We’ll review task completion, errors, and time to book before deciding what to change.
check: 列出决定下一步的反馈或指标

blockers: 人工听审音频，核对文本、语速和停顿。
真实账号进度保存与生产页面逐期验收。
